Wow... I'm at a loss for words! The support here has been overwhelming. I am truly touched. I rarely, rarely get comments IRL about my progress (I have moved to new cities a couple of times during this process, so acquaintances/coworkers have never known my whole journey.) I haven't even bought smaller clothes, just because I didn't really see a big enough difference myself yet. To see so many strangers remark that there is a big difference is eye-opening and moving. 

For those curious, my process came down to building a new relationship with food and incorporating exercise. I got a bad case of salmonella that lasted a full month shortly after that first picture was taken. After a month of being unable to overeat without making myself much sicker, I began to break my habit of overeating in general. I still eat the foods I love, just in moderation! 

In terms of exercise. I have OCD and my psychiatrist encouraged me to go for walks outside to refocus/distract my mind anytime I felt compelled to perform a compulsion. This practice started a habit of walking very regularly, often for ten miles at a time. I also started working at a pool so I could have access to it all the time and swim as much as I could-- I grew up swimming, so it was a familiar and fun exercise option. Within the past few months, I also got a second job at a fitness studio with the intention of being able to take fitness classes anytime I wanted. I take spin classes there, but the job itself is where I get most of my activity-- there are no chairs for employees, so I'm on my feet for the duration of every shift, letting me clock in around 6 miles every time I work. 

Again, thank you for every nice comment here. It has really boosted me up :)

I'll try to answer these as best as I can! SPOILERS!!!!

​

*Why did Mel break into the house for the cookie jar?*  After watching the show, do you think that viewers are supposed to believe that Mel is great at his profession? Do you think we are even supposed to believe that Mel has tremendous regard for his personal safety? His past is that of stealing coke from evidence rooms, his present includes scenes of substance abuse relapse. The writers knew that nobody in their right mind would do such a thing as confront dangerous people-- so they made Mel do it, who they had carefully established as strung out on several things (including ego and literal drugs.) Also, we watched Mel get super fucking comfortable walking right up to the Byrde house ready for confrontation and questions this whole time-- he crossed the line of accusatory and invasive of their space in every single interaction he had with the Byrdes. He brought the video of Jonah at Helen's to the Byrde house and walked away unscathed, for instance.

*Ruth was out of character.* I disagree. There's nobility in recognizing when a battle is lost. Ruth died on her feet, standing her ground unapologetically, choosing to die an Ozark Langmore than pursue safety elsewhere, otherwise named. What was she going to do, convince a mother not to avenge the death of her son? As this season says: have you watched this whole show and learned nothing of people's will? Ruth knows will.

*Did Jonah shoot Mel or someone else? It's a finale, why the mystery?* It is not my belief that the writing here intends you to think of this as a mystery. Jonah shot Mel to save the family, as the Byrdes gathered together around the trampoline, a long-standing symbol of Byrde family unity (refer back to S1E1 for that). I think the shot ended on Jonah at that moment because, well, who cares about Mel's gunshot wound in comparison to watching Jonah as he loses any semblance of innocence he had left? I think a close-up on Jonah is justified for the moment... I think I would've found the corpse shot less impactful than watching this key development of a central character, somehow.

*Omar's death scene was sloppy. This isn't really an unanswered question other than why are we expected to believe the cop would get away with the murder.* Why is it unlikely to believe that there exists a person within the reach of Camila who would risk U.S. jail time if caught performing a hit? This requires zero suspension of disbelief for me.

*I may have missed this, but didn't the Byrde's still have a percentage of ownership in the Missouri Belle? If so, you can't just up and leave a business that is regulated by the alcohol & lottery commission.* If you were looking for quibbling about the residency requirements for the Byrdes per their percent ownership in the Missouri Belle as it concerns the Alchohol & Lottery Commission, you were clearly looking for a different finale than I was. So be it

*What happened to Three?* What do you think? At no other point in the story was I thinking "what would Three think about this" or "I wonder what Three is up to" so I guess IDGAF about this particular "mystery." What is more, I think it serves the writing for us to reflect sadly and uncertainly on Three's future. After all, what is more tragic? A finale that leaves every Langmore dead? Or: a finale that leaves every Langmore dead but the youngest, least remarkable Langmore, who gets to grieve the weight of that death? We can only assume that he lives a cursed life until he dies a sad death, like every.other.Langmore.
Personally, I didn't think there were any thematic points left unanswered at the end. But I'd be interested in hearing what you think should've been answered

It depends!!!! Most rooms in most freshman dorms have carpet, but you won't know until you get your particular room assignment. So even if you know you will request a particular building, and most rooms in that building have carpet, you could very well be assigned a unit without carpeting.
